findings: l.2621-2622 ('up to finite index, L(Gamma) preserves an isotropic vector v0 and Gamma contains a parabolic element gamma_1') does not follow from Prop 9.1: Barbot's proof (l.2585-2594) produces a parabolic element of the Zariski closure G0, not of Gamma; 9.1 allows L(Gamma') fixing v0 and consisting of elliptic elements only, a branch §9 never treats.

The lemma `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` as previously stated (no discreteness) is FALSE for d >= 5: Gamma generated by the linear isometries with NolParams (L_a,0,0,0,0), (L_b,0,e,0,0) on Minkowski 5 (P0bar = R^4 = H, L_q z = q z, a, b a free pair of unit quaternions, e != 0) is all-elliptic, fixes v0 = ofNull 1 0 0, and no finite-index subgroup fixes a timelike vector (a common fixed point of lambda(gamma_a^k), lambda(gamma_b^m) would be 0, and lambda(gamma_b^m) 0 = (L_b^m - 1)(L_b - 1)^-1 e != 0). The counterexample is documented (SCOPE finding (7)), NOT formalized: it needs the freeness of the quaternion pair. It is not a holonomy group (it fixes 0, and it is not discrete in Isom(M^n)).

The true form needs an argument absent from the paper: for Gamma DISCRETE in Isom(M^n) with L(Gamma) fixing a null v0 and all elliptic, (i) Gamma lies in the amenable group of isometries whose linear part fixes v0, so contains no free group of rank 2; (ii) Tits' alternative makes it virtually solvable; (iii) its rotation parts on P0bar are then virtually in a torus; (iv) commutators have trivial rotation part, hence unipotent and elliptic linear part, hence trivial: L(Gamma) is virtually abelian (the external `TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull`); (v) commuting elliptic linear parts fix a common timelike vector (PROVED, `exists_timelike_fixed_of_comm_elliptic`, any d). Barbot's Gamma is discrete (proved from Cor 8.2's properness on Sigma, `discreteTopology_of_ccAction`).

Second fixer pass (2026-11-01). The dispatch's premise (the lemma false as stated) is already discharged: since round 3a (commit 43a8725) `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` carries `DiscreteTopology Γ` and `TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d` and is PROVED; it is true in that form. Option (a) with `λ(Γ)` discrete is NOT available at the call sites: they supply `Γ` discrete in Isom(M^n) only (`discreteTopology_of_developsCC`); Barbot's own commented example (GHFspace.tex l.2551–2562) is a discrete group whose linear part is not discrete, and point (3) (l.2660–2663, l.2674–2675) gives `α(Γ)` discrete in Aff(Q0), which mixes `u` and `v` and does not make `λ(Γ)` (the `(R, v)` action on P0bar) discrete.

Option (b) cannot close the branch from what Prop 9.1 cites: the linear counterexample (free unit-quaternion pair on P0bar = R^4) satisfies `BenoistNoLox`'s conclusion (it fixes v0), and its Zariski closure contains null rotations (the closure of λ(Γ) contains z ↦ b z and z ↦ b z + e, hence z ↦ z + e), so the step 'G0 admits only elliptic elements, therefore compact' (l.2596–2597) never fires; an 'elliptic analogue of Benoist' (all elliptic in Γ ⇒ all elliptic in the Zariski closure) is FALSE. The Barbot-cited external that reaches the branch is Thm 5.1 (Auslander–Carrière–Dal'bo, l.1697–1704), which uses Γ's discreteness: it makes Γ_nd nilpotent, and a nilpotent group of elliptic linear parts fixes a common timelike vector (PROVED, `exists_timelike_fixed_of_nilpotent_elliptic`, every d, upper central series), so Γ_nd's linear parts fix one (`exists_timelike_fixed_nonDiscretePart`) and the branch closes when Γ_nd has finite index in Γ (`exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_ausl`). The residual case (L(Γ) meeting infinitely many components of its closure) is where only the non-Barbot Tits/amenability argument helps.

The counterexample stays a documented finding, not a theorem: no torsion counterexample exists (a torsion linear group is locally finite (Schur), its rotation parts in SO(n−2) are virtually abelian (Jordan), commutators are then elliptic translations of P0bar, i.e. trivial, and the commuting case applies), so every counterexample contains a free group (Tits) and its formalization needs a free pair in SU(2) (e.g. the Banach–Tarski pair lifted), a multi-hundred-line development.

findings: 'quotients of M^n by a group of translations by spacelike translation vectors' (l.588-590) is not 'translations whose span is spacelike' (BARBOT-THEOREMS §1's reading, Examples' IsTranslationSpacetime): in M^4 the translations by e1 and e0 + e2 + sqrt2 e1 generate a rank-2 group all of whose nonzero vectors are spacelike while its span contains the null vector e0 + e2 (`spacelike_translations_null_span`). Its quotient carries no invariant entire acausal graph (an invariant graph f = x2 + h, h doubly periodic, cannot be strictly contracting along e2), so (CC') should exclude it, but [9.E]'s 'translation spacetime' then needs that argument.

Closer pass (2026-11-01): Barbot states only freeness of Gamma on M^n (l.2609-2610); the quotient needs properness, proved here for every subgroup whose linear parts fix a timelike v (`CCAction.finite_of_fix_timelike`: the v-lines carry a compact of M^n into a compact of Sigma, Sigma being a 1-Lipschitz entire graph). The degenerate-span danger (`spacelike_translations_null_span`) is excluded by ACAUSALITY ALONE, not by (CC')'s null saturation, once the null direction n of the span is recurrent (some s >= 1 and translation tau of a point p0 of Sigma with |s n - tau| < eps): `not_null_recurrent_of_isEntireAcausalGraph`; the example group itself preserves no entire acausal graph (`not_isEntireAcausalGraph_null_span`, via Dirichlet). Recurrence for a lattice of the span (pigeonhole in the torus) is the only unformalized link of that argument.

labels.label: rem choixcoord (Rem 9.2, l.2737-2760)
findings: Rem 9.2's changes of vn are not changes of null frame: |vn + w|^2 = |w|^2 for w in P0bar and |vn + a v0|^2 = 2a (`frameChange_null`). The correct change is vn' = vn + w - (|w|^2/2) v0, i.e. the coordinates (x, z, y) -> (x + <w|z> - (y/2)|w|^2, z - y w, y), the action of (id, 0, -w, 0, 0) in A(v0); under it u' = u, v' = v and Barbot's mu' = mu + <u|w> hold exactly (`choixcoord`). The first bullet (w in Delta0) is not a frame change at all.

kb_proposals: Barbot's null coordinates are a model `ℝ × E × ℝ` with `Q = 2xy + |z|²` (`Flat/Nonloxodromic`'s `nolQ`, `NolParam`), linked to `𝐌ⁿ` by `nolToMink := ofNull`; an element of `Stab(v₀)` is the data `(R, u, v, μ, b)` with an explicit composition law (`NolParam.mul`), and powers/quadratic leading terms are proved by `ext` + `ring` after `norm_add_sq_real`, keeping `‖u + y • v‖²` as an atom.

To extend a partial linear map from a subspace E by zero on a complement, glue with `LinearPMap.sup` and evaluate through `LinearPMap.sup_apply`; `E ⊔ Fᗮ = ⊤` is easiest through `(E ⊔ Fᗮ)ᗮ = Eᗮ ⊓ F = ⊥` (`Submodule.inf_orthogonal`, `orthogonal_orthogonal`, `orthogonal_eq_bot_iff`).
`Σ` is a reserved token in Lean 4 (sigma types): it cannot be a variable name; nor can `y₋` (subscript minus).

A uniform power lands in a finite-index subgroup without normal cores: `Subgroup.pow_mem_of_relIndex_ne_zero_of_dvd hidx ha (fun _ hm hle => Nat.dvd_factorial hm hle)` gives a ^ (H.relIndex K)! ∈ H for every a ∈ K; conjugates are handled by `conj_pow`.

The built Develop.olean (2026-10-31 23:50) predates the closer's Develop.lean edits (it lacks `isElliptic_linOf_zpow_iff`, `IsParabolic.zpow_linOf`, and `ccAction_of_developsCC`/`bprop_danom` there take no `[T2Space M]`); a downstream file must use names absent from both and carry `[T2Space M]` as an explicit binder so that it typechecks against either olean.

A group of isometries acting properly on a nonempty closed invariant subset of Minkowski space is discrete in Externals' `isomTopology` (`discreteTopology_of_ccAction`): bound gamma x near gamma0 x, use properness on the compact Sigma ∩ (closedBall x 1 ∪ closedBall (gamma0 x) 1), then {gamma0} = U \ (U \ {gamma0}) with U open and finite (T2 from `isomPair_injective`).

Commuting elliptic Lorentz maps fix a common timelike vector: induct on the dimension of an invariant subspace W containing a timelike vector; W ⊕ W^⊥ (`isCompl_orthogonal_iff_disjoint minkForm_isRefl`, W^⊥ spacelike) and the W-part of a fixed timelike vector is fixed (`exists_timelike_fixed_mem_of_invariant`).

A nilpotent group of elliptic Lorentz maps fixes a common timelike vector: induct along `Subgroup.upperCentralSeries` (at this pin in namespace `Subgroup`; the `Group.` names are deprecated), with W_k the common fixed space of Z_k (Γ-invariant as Z_k is characteristic, hence normal), on which Z_{k+1} commutes because ⁅a, b⁆ ∈ Z_k (`mem_upperCentralSeries_succ_iff`, `commutatorElement_def`); the commuting step is the relative `exists_timelike_fixed_of_comm_elliptic_on`.

A group whose linear parts fix a timelike v acts properly on all of M^n as soon as it acts properly on an invariant entire acausal graph Sigma: push a compact K along v into Sigma (`exists_compact_lift_of_entire`: |s|(v_0 - |v_bar|) <= |k_0 - g(k_bar)| for k + s v in graph g), and use gamma(k + s v) = gamma k + s v (`isom_smul_add_smul`). Gives ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul/IsCancelSMul on the subtype top and `FlatQuotient.toFlatSpacetime`.

When a fan-out lemma's dispatched statement is refuted (here [9.U]'s exists_unipotent_restriction), integrate through ONE sorry'd lemma in the corrected form whose conclusion is reusable verbatim (Nonlox.UnipotentRestrictionConclusion after a frame psi), compose frames (psi*phi) downstream, and say in the docstring that the corrected form's truth is open; never state the refuted form as a theorem.

NO STATEMENT CHANGED IN THIS PASS: every existing declaration keeps its signature and conclusion, so Classification.lean (which already consumes the round-3a forms — `TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull`, `titsVirtuallyAbelianNull_zero`, `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null hT (discreteTopology_of_developsCC hpair h hle₁) hv0 hv hfix hell`, `nonloxodromic hB hT hBieb …`) needs NO change. The statement changes in force are those of round 3a (commit 43a8725), recorded in `statement_changes`: (1) `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` OLD `{Γ} {v₀} (_hv0 : v₀ ≠ 0) (_hv : minkQ v₀ = 0) (_hfix : ∀ γ ∈ Γ, linOf γ v₀ = v₀) (_hell : ∀ γ ∈ Γ, IsElliptic (linOf γ)) : ∃ Γ' ≤ Γ, Γ'.relIndex Γ ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ v, minkQ v < 0 ∧ ∀ γ ∈ Γ', linOf γ v = v` [sorry, false for d ≥ 5] → NEW `(hT : TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d) {Γ} (hdisc : DiscreteTopology Γ) {v₀} (hv0) (hv) (hfix) (hell) : <same conclusion>` [proved]; (2) `nonloxodromic` OLD `(hB : BenoistNoLox d) (hBieb …) (hpair) (hcaus) (h) (hnl) : <C>` → NEW `(hB : BenoistNoLox d) (hT : TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d) (hBieb …) (hpair) (hcaus) (h) (hnl) : <C, unchanged>`. WHAT THIS PASS DID (DEC-27 options checked): (a) `λ(Γ)` discrete is not supplied by the call sites (only Γ is discrete; Barbot's commented example l.2551–2562; point (3) l.2660–2675 concerns α(Γ)), so no λ-discrete form was added; (b) no external faithful to Prop 9.1's citation (Benoist) can give the conclusion — the linear counterexample satisfies BenoistNoLox and its Zariski closure has null rotations — so none was added; the Barbot-cited Thm 5.1 (AuslanderCarriereDalbo, already in Externals) gives the branch on Γ_nd; (c) ADDED, all proved, no sorry, no axiom: `exists_timelike_fixed_of_comm_elliptic_on` (relative commuting lemma), `linFixSub` (common fixed subspace, a Submodule), `exists_timelike_fixed_of_nilpotent_elliptic` ([Group.IsNilpotent Γ], elliptic linear parts ⇒ common timelike fixed vector, every d), `exists_timelike_fixed_nonDiscretePart` (AuslanderCarriereDalbo d, DiscreteTopology Γ, elliptic ⇒ Γ_nd's linear parts fix a timelike vector), `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_ausl` (+ `(nonDiscretePart Γ).relIndex Γ ≠ 0` ⇒ the conclusion of `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null`, with no null vector and no Tits). `nonloxodromic` keeps the Tits route (switching would add a hypothesis the §8 data do not supply). Counterexample: documented (SCOPE finding (7), extended), not formalized (any counterexample contains a free group). `nonloxodromic_elliptic`, `nonloxodromic_parabolic`: unchanged statements, still sorried, tags unchanged — each needs multi-hundred-line developments (isomTopology a group topology so that the discrete Γ' is closed and acts properly on M^n; the bundled quotient; the Bieberbach transport to E ≃ᵃⁱ E; RestrictsIn for suspendre; for the parabolic one the frame change, [9.b] for R ≠ id, [9.U] and Ω := π_U⁻¹(Ω_A)). Docstring: bprop:sanloxo bullet, the branch section comment, the checklist row and SCOPE finding (7) extended. Sorries 2. PREVIOUS NOTES (round 3a and earlier): FIXER PASS (bprop:sanloxo branch) 2026-11-01. STATEMENT CHANGES (DEC-27, this file only; see `statement_changes`): (1) `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` gains `(hT : TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d)` (first explicit argument) and `(hdisc : DiscreteTopology Γ)` (after Γ, in Externals' scoped `isomTopology`); conclusion unchanged; now PROVED (was a sorry, false for d ≥ 5). (2) `nonloxodromic` gains `(hT : TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d)` as its second explicit argument (after hB); conclusion unchanged. No other statement changed; `nonloxodromic_elliptic` and `nonloxodromic_parabolic` unchanged (still sorried, tags kept; the [9.E] tag now notes the proved discreteness). NEW DECLS: external `TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d : Prop` (∀ Γ discrete, linear parts fixing a nonzero null v₀ and all elliptic ⇒ ∃ finite-index Γ' ≤ Γ with pairwise commuting linear parts; derivation from Tits' alternative + amenability + compact solvable groups in its docstring; not cited by Barbot) with witness `titsVirtuallyAbelianNull_zero`; proved: `exists_timelike_fixed_of_comm_elliptic` (commuting elliptic linear parts fix a common timelike vector, any d), `exists_timelike_fixed_mem_of_invariant`, `disjoint_minkOrth_of_timelike`, `isCompl_minkOrth_of_timelike`, `continuous_isom_smul_apply`, `discreteTopology_of_ccAction` (CCAction Γ St ⇒ DiscreteTopology Γ), `discreteTopology_of_developsCC` (hpair h, Γ' ≤ ρ.range ⇒ DiscreteTopology Γ'). FOR CLASSIFICATION (its closer runs next): `caseOutput_nonloxodromic` (Classification.lean ~l.344) calls `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null hv0 hv hfix hell`, which no longer typechecks; replace by `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null hT (discreteTopology_of_developsCC hpair h hle₁) hv0 hv hfix hell`, with `hT : TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull d` added to `caseOutput_nonloxodromic` and supplied from `BarbotExternals` (a new field, e.g. `tits : ∀ k ≤ d, TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull k`; `barbotExternals_zero` extends with `titsVirtuallyAbelianNull_zero`, and `BarbotExternals.mono` with the same pattern as `benoist`). Any direct call of `nonloxodromic` must insert hT after hB. The counterexample to the old lemma is documented (SCOPE finding (7), REPORT bprop:sanloxo findings), not formalized (needs freeness of a pair of unit quaternions). Sorries now 2. No name collision with any scaffold source (grep). PREVIOUS: CLOSER PASS 2026-11-01: 0 sorries closed, 3 left. (a) `exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null` is FALSE AS STATED for d >= 5: counterexample (2-generated, linear, from a free pair of unit quaternions acting on P0bar = R^4 = H) in the bprop:sanloxo sorry entry, in the Lean tag and in the SCOPE finding (7); the statement was not changed; the old obstruction's 'finitely generated suffices' is also refuted; true for d <= 3 and for discrete lambda(Gamma). `nonloxodromic`'s third branch and Classification.lean:314 consume it: raise with the orchestrator. (b) `nonloxodromic_elliptic` and (c) `nonloxodromic_parabolic` keep their obstruction tags unchanged: each still needs developments not in the library (properness of Gamma'' on Omega(S~) and the bundled FlatSpacetime quotient; the transport of Gamma' to E ≃ᵃⁱ E and BieberbachI/BieberbachMaxConclusion; RestrictsIn for suspendre after an index-2 passage; for (b) the exclusion of degenerate translation spans from (CC'); for (c) a frame taking v0 to ofNull 1 0 0, [9.b] for R != id, the [9.U] Bieberbach step and lattice/linearity of u, the y-origin change, the extension of nu, and Omega := pi_U^-1(Omega_A) with D(M~) ⊆ Omega). Neither was found false. No statement, signature or docstring claim changed; only the first sorry's tag and SCOPE (two additions) were edited. PREVIOUS (fixer pass): FIXER PASS 2026-11-01 (audit blocking 1, 2 and minors applied). (1) `nonloxodromic_parabolic` restated: its earlier conclusion (M(S) = Gamma''\Omega(S~) an LTP over a spacetime embedding in a unipotent one) is refuted by Rem 9.4; it now gives ∃ Gamma'' ≤ Gamma' of finite index, Omega : Opens with range D ⊆ Omega ⊆ Omega(S~), B with IsQuotientOf B Gamma'' Omega, and IsLTPOver B M1 with IsUnipotentSpacetime M1 (DEC-43 R1, l.3126). `nonloxodromic` now outputs ∃ Gamma'' ≤ Gamma (finite index) Omega B, range D ⊆ Omega ⊆ Omega(S~) ∧ IsQuotientOf B Gamma'' Omega ∧ ((Omega = Omega(S~) ∧ LTP over a translation spacetime) ∨ LTP over a unipotent spacetime); still no sorry of its own (range D ⊆ Omega(S~) from bprop_danom in the elliptic branch). (2) Both branch theorems gained `Gamma'.relIndex rho.range != 0`; the parabolic one also `hnl` on rho.range. (3) The G6 bridge is proved (`linOf_fix_of_relIndex`, `perp_invariant_omegaS_of_developsCC`). (4) Checklist tag '⚠ strengthened' for the fixed frame. All main theorems carry `[T2Space M]` (explicit binder). The output (2) of the dispatch for Classification is false as worded and must be replaced by this file's form — raise with the orchestrator. Remaining sorries: 3 (exists_timelike_fixed_of_elliptic_of_null, nonloxodromic_elliptic, nonloxodromic_parabolic); none could be closed in this pass (Bieberbach transport, suspendre, quotient constructions and the [9.U] steps are each multi-hundred-line developments). Typechecked against the built oleans; the closer's newer Develop.lean adds `[T2Space M]` to `ccAction_of_developsCC`/`bprop_danom`, which this file supplies, so it should also typecheck after Develop is rebuilt (not verified: no lake build). Universe: B, M1 : FlatSpacetime.{0}. No public-name collision with any scaffold source (checked by grep against current sources, incl. Loxodromic.lean and the edited Develop.lean). CLOSER PASS (WP-34c, 2026-11-01): NO STATEMENT CHANGED; sorry count stays 2. [9.E] item (1) CLOSED as lemmas: free proper action of every Gamma'' <= Gamma' on M^n and the bundled quotient B = Gamma''\Omega(S~) (`exists_isQuotientOf_omegaS_of_fix_timelike`, `CCAction.finite_of_fix_timelike`, `CCAction.free_of_fix_timelike`, the subtype instances). [9.E] item (4): the null-span exclusion reduced to recurrence (`not_null_recurrent_of_isEntireAcausalGraph`, acausality only), with the SCOPE-finding-3 example group shown to preserve no entire acausal graph (`not_isEntireAcausalGraph_null_span`). Item (3) sharpened: no index-2 passage is needed in [9.E] (Gamma'' acts on U by translations). Still open in [9.E]: (2) Bieberbach transport to E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E and the maximal U, (3) ι/RestrictsIn/suspendre assembly, (4) torus recurrence for a lattice + the frame moving the spacelike span to {t = 0} + the identification restrictGroup Gamma'' = frameConj phi (horizGroup Lambda). [9.P]–[9.A]: untouched, its seven missing items are each multi-hundred-line developments (frame transitivity on null rays in SO_0(1,d) needs spatial SO(d) rotations, which the library does not construct; [9.b] for R ≠ id; [9.U] Bieberbach/maximality; the y-normalisation; ℓ; the Ω_A construction and the quotients). No counterexample found to either sorried statement. INTEGRATOR PASS (DEC-50, 2026-11-01): docstrings only, no code; see integrator_DEC50. The external TitsVirtuallyAbelianNull is now proved in Flat/TitsNull and discharged in Flat/Classification.

integrator_WP34c.statement_changes: none (every existing declaration keeps its signature, binder names included; only docstrings and the two proofs changed)
integrator_WP34c.planner_sketch_deviation: The planner's WireP used P3 = exists_unipotent_restriction verbatim; the fan-out module UnipotentRestriction proves that statement FALSE (not_unipotentRestrictionStatement), so it could not be imported as a theorem. The wiring instead uses exists_unipotent_restriction_up_to_frame (P3's hypotheses; its conclusion Nonlox.UnipotentRestrictionConclusion for (frameConj psi G, psi • Sigma) for some psi) and runs the rest of WireP in the composite frame psi*phi: P5's hD only needs (linOf (psi*phi))^-1 (ofNull 1 0 0) null and nonzero (any null line through D(M~) meets Sigma), and hSt reads nullY on (psi*phi) • Sigma directly, so no constraint on psi is needed. The nine bookkeeping obligations of WireP are all discharged (CCAction under frameConj; the frame group fixes ofNull 1 0 0; IsParabolic.conj; acausality from (CC'); hach through nolQ_nonneg_of_isAcausal and AffineMinkEmbedding.apply_sub; hΓ in NolParam form; frameConj (psi*phi) (frameConj (psi*phi)^-1 G'') = G''; range D ⊆ D(Sigma); d = 0 vacuous).
integrator_WP34c.collision_check: grep over Causal/ and scaffold/: the three new public names are unique; the frameConj helpers are private because Cla/UnipEnvelope (which imports this file) has Causal.Flat.Cla.frameConj_inv_frameConj / frameConj_mul'. The Nonlox modules declare only Causal.Flat.Nonlox.* names (and two instances on the type synonym EllTl), so importing them adds no unqualified names to downstream files; no downstream file opens Nonlox.
